questions.stem: A question returns a fluent answer from the wrong passage, and the team wants to find which stage failed. What should they do first?

options.text: Switch to a larger model and read a few more answers
options.says: Ruled out because "Fluent output hides that", and a larger model reads the same retrieved passages.

options.text: Measure recall at k on a set with known source documents
options.says: The page says "The way to see it is to measure retrieval on its own", with questions "whose source documents are known".

options.text: Lengthen the prompt with more rules about citing sources
options.says: Ruled out because the failure sits in what was retrieved: "the passage with the answer never reached the prompt".

options.text: Raise the temperature to see whether another passage appears
options.says: Ruled out because temperature changes the wording of the answer, and "A fluent answer can come from the wrong passage".

questions.stem: A passage reads "The company's revenue grew by 3% over the previous quarter" and matches many unrelated questions. Which fix does the write-up describe?

options.text: Prepend a sentence of explanatory context before indexing it
options.says: The page says to prepend "chunk-specific explanatory context to each chunk before embedding" and before building the keyword index.

options.text: Shorten it to a single sentence of three or four words
options.says: Ruled out because the problem is lost surroundings: "A chunk lifted out of its document can lose its meaning."

options.text: Delete it and rely on the model's own knowledge of the firm
options.says: Ruled out because the fix keeps the chunk: the model is asked "to write that sentence for each chunk".

options.text: Embed it twice and average the two vectors that result
options.says: Ruled out because the fix is that "the chunk is indexed as a short sentence of context followed by the text", and a doubled vector adds no information.

questions.stem: A keyword index and an embedding index disagree on the best chunk for a query. Why is a hybrid usually better than either alone?

options.text: They miss different questions, so merging the results keeps what each finds
options.says: The page says "The two indexes fail on different questions, which is why most systems use both."

options.text: Their scores share one scale, which makes adding them a sound choice
options.says: Ruled out because "the scores cannot be added" when they sit on different scales.

options.text: The embedding side handles exact strings well, and the keyword side adds speed
options.says: Ruled out because "BM25 is exact", and the embedding "is weaker with exact strings".

options.text: The merge makes chunking of the documents unnecessary for later stages
options.says: Ruled out because "A chunk is a window of words", and the merge works on chunks that already exist.

questions.stem: A team reads a published failure-rate drop of 67% and promises the same drop to a customer. What is wrong with the promise?

options.text: The figure applies only to embeddings, which the customer does not use
options.says: Ruled out because the 67% row is "Those two, with reranking added", so it is not embeddings alone.

options.text: The figure is too small to be useful for any real system that is deployed
options.says: Ruled out because the figures "show an order of magnitude and a ranking of the techniques".

options.text: The figure comes from the source's datasets, and yours needs measuring
options.says: The page says "These are the write-up's figures, measured on its datasets" and "Measure your own."

options.text: The figure was measured with a retired model that no longer exists
options.says: Ruled out because "The percentages for contextual retrieval below are Anthropic's measurements on its own datasets", and the page names no model.
